policy_title: Implement Planned Social Care Reforms and Multi-Year Funding
stated: The Conservative Party will implement planned reforms to cap social care costs from October 2025, provide local authorities with a multi-year funding settlement for social care at the next Spending Review, and take forward reforms from the 'People at the Heart of Care' White Paper.

source.quote: We will implement our planned reforms to cap social care costs from October 2025. We will invest in more and better facilities, continuing to deliver 40 new hospitals by 2030 and investing proportionately more in out-of-hospital services over time. ...At the next Spending Review, we will give local authorities a multi-year funding settlement to support social care and will take forward the reforms in our ‘People at the Heart of Care’ White Paper.

bearing_set.reason: Directly addresses social care access, cost caps, and funding adequacy for older and disabled people — core O8 indicators.
Social care workforce reforms (from 'People at the Heart of Care') bear on pay, conditions, and job quality for care workers — a large, low-paid workforce.

NHS delayed-discharge (bed-blocking) is materially driven by inadequate social care capacity; better-funded social care directly reduces this bottleneck, moving the NHS waiting-list and A&E-flow indicators.

The Dilnot care cap was costed at several billion pounds per year by 2030 and multi-year local-authority settlements add further committed expenditure; whether this spending is funded or borrowed materially affects the debt-path sustainability indicator.

membership_note: Three clear bearings: O8 is the primary target (care cost protection and access), O3 is a well-evidenced secondary effect via the NHS-social care interface, and O12 reflects the non-negligible fiscal commitment the reforms represent.
